Q: Where can I find a community that will be like the old stack overflow with showcases and so on? A:

I think you might be confusing SO with someplace else. I've been here for 16 year, and I have no memory of anything like what you are describing. it has always been Q&A. Early on, there was dumb stuff like 'boat programming,' and more tolerance for somewhat mushier questions, but not 'sharing interesting projects' etc.

Q: Serve two https hostnames from single node process & port A:

You are correct: https.createServer({ key, cert }) gives you only one certificate pair per listener, unless you use SNI.

The key point is that certificate selection happens during the TLS handshake, before there is any HTTP request. That means you cannot switch certificates based on the HTTP Host header. You must switch certificates based on the SNI servername. Node supports this with SNICallback (and internally with per-host TLS contexts).

If you want the most plug-and-play solution in Node (no Nginx, no Apache), use roster-server. It is explicitly described as “a domain host router to host multiple HTTPS” and it depends on greenlock-express for automated TLS handling.

Q: why I can't use the pointer in place of index in an array to return the value and express the position of index? A:

You can use a pointer to access an array element’s value,
but you cannot replace an index with a pointer to represent the position in a safe and meaningful way — because a pointer stores an address, not a logical position.

Q: Sudden Docker error about "client API version" A:

I was running a Docker in Docker (DinD) container in the Kubernetes cluster and I recently upgraded it to version 29.1.5-dind. After that upgrade, I started getting the following error:

Error response from daemon: client version 1.41 is too old. Minimum supported API version is 1.44, please upgrade your client to a newer version

I fixed it by setting DOCKER_MIN_API_VERSION to 1.41 in the environment variables.

New code snippet looks like this:

.
.
.
spec:
  containers:
    - name: docker
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      image: "docker:29.1.5-dind"
      command:
        - dockerd
      args:
        - --host=unix:///var/run/docker.sock
        - --storage-driver=overlay2
        - --mtu=1380
        - --group=999
      env:
        - name: "DOCKER_MIN_API_VERSION"
          value: "1.41"
.
.
.

Reference: Docker Engine v29 - Blog
